title.zh: 卷九十六 志第四十五上: 食貨四
title.raw: 卷九十六 志第四十五上: 食貨四 Volume 96 Treatises 49: Finance and Economics 4

sentences.zh: 食貨四 ○俸秩

translations.literal: Finance and Economics 4 ○ Salaries and Ranks
translations.idiomatic: Finance and Economics, Part Four: Salaries and Official Ranks

sentences.zh: 官必有祿，所以養廉也。

translations.literal: Officials must have salary, thereby to nurture integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Every officeholder must receive a salary, for that is how the state sustains honest conduct.

sentences.zh: 元初未置祿秩，世祖既位之初，首命給之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuan no salary ranks were established; when Shizu had just taken the throne, he first ordered them to be granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yuan no formal salary scales existed; as soon as Kublai Khan took the throne, granting salaries was among his first orders.

sentences.zh: 內而朝臣百司，外而路府州縣，微而府史胥徒，莫不有祿。

translations.literal: Within, court ministers and the hundred offices; without, circuits, prefectures, districts, and counties; down to clerks and runners in government offices—none lacked salary.
translations.idiomatic: From court ministers and central agencies inward to circuit, prefectural, and county officials outward, and even down to petty clerks and runners, every post carried pay.

sentences.zh: 大德中，以外有司有職田，於是無職田者，復益之以俸米。

translations.literal: In the Dade era, because outer offices had official lands, those without official lands were again supplemented with salary rice.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dade reign, since officials posted outside the capital often held official land allotments, those who had none were given an additional rice allowance on top of their cash salary.

sentences.zh: 其所以養官吏者，不亦厚乎！

translations.literal: The means by which officials are supported—is it not generous!
translations.idiomatic: The state’s provision for its officials was nothing if not generous.

sentences.zh: 祿秩之制，凡朝廷職官，中統元年定之；

translations.literal: As for the system of salaries and ranks, all court offices were fixed in the first year of Zhongtong;
translations.idiomatic: The salary system for the bureaucracy was laid down in stages: court offices in the first year of the Zhongtong era (1260);

sentences.zh: 六部官，二年定之；

translations.literal: the Six Ministries in the second year;
translations.idiomatic: the Six Ministries in the second year;

sentences.zh: 隨路州縣官，是年十月定之。

translations.literal: circuit, prefecture, and county officials in the tenth month of that year.
translations.idiomatic: and circuit, prefectural, and county officials in the tenth month of that same year.

sentences.zh: 至元六年，又分上中下縣，為三等。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhiyuan, counties were again divided into upper, middle, and lower, as three grades.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 6 (1269), counties were further classified into upper, middle, and lower grades for pay purposes.

sentences.zh: 提刑按察司官吏，六年定之。

translations.literal: Officials of the Surveillance Commission were fixed in the sixth year.
translations.idiomatic: Salaries for the regional surveillance commissions were set in the sixth year.

sentences.zh: 自經歷以下，七年復增之。

translations.literal: From the registrar downward, in the seventh year they were again increased.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, pay for registrars and ranks below them was raised again.

sentences.zh: 轉運司官及諸匠官，七年定之。

translations.literal: Transport Commission officials and various craft officials were fixed in the seventh year.
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissioners and various craft-office officials received their scales in the seventh year.

sentences.zh: 其運司依民官例，於差發內支給。

translations.literal: The transport offices, following the civil-official precedent, were paid from within corvée assignments.
translations.idiomatic: Transport offices, treated like civil local officials, were paid out of corvée-assignment funds.

sentences.zh: 至十七年，定奪俸祿，凡內外官吏皆住支。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, salaries were adjudicated and fixed; all inner and outer officials ceased payment.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 17 (1280), salaries were reassessed and payment to all officials, court and local, was suspended.

sentences.zh: 十八年，更命公事畢而無罪者給之，公事未畢而有罪者逐之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, it was further ordered: those whose public business was finished and who were without guilt received payment; those whose public business was unfinished and who had guilt were expelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year a new rule applied: salary was paid only after an assignment was completed and the holder cleared of wrongdoing; those still under investigation or found guilty were dismissed without pay.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，重定百官俸，始於各品分上中下三例，視職事為差，事大者依上例，事小者依中例。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, salaries of the hundred offices were again fixed; for each grade upper, middle, and lower examples were first established, differing according to duties—great affairs followed the upper example, lesser affairs the middle.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 22 (1285) official salaries were overhauled: each rank was given upper, middle, and lower rates, with the rate chosen according to how weighty the post was.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，又命內外官吏俸以十分為率，添支五分。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, it was again ordered that inner and outer officials’ salaries, taking ten parts as the standard, receive an additional payment of five parts.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year all officials received a fifty-percent supplement on top of their base salary.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，定各處儒學教授俸，與蒙古、醫學同。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, salaries of Confucian-school instructors in each place were fixed, the same as Mongolian and medical schools.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year the pay of Confucian-school professors throughout the realm was set equal to that of instructors in Mongolian and medical schools.

sentences.zh: 成宗大德三年，詔益小吏俸米。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dade under Chengzong, an edict increased salary rice for petty clerks.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 3 (1299) Emperor Chengzong ordered an increase in the rice allowance for junior clerical staff.

sentences.zh: 六年，又定各處行省、宣慰司、致用院、宣撫司、茶鹽運司、鐵冶都提舉司、淘金總管府、銀場提舉司等官循行俸例。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, salaries of provincial administrations, pacification commissions, revenue-use offices, pacification superintendencies, tea-and-salt transport offices, iron-smelting directorates-general, gold-panning chief agencies, silver-mine superintendencies, and the like in each place were again fixed to follow the salary precedents.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year standard salary tables were extended to provincial administrations, pacification commissions, revenue offices, tea-and-salt transport bureaus, iron and gold agencies, silver-mine offices, and comparable posts nationwide.

sentences.zh: 七年，始加給內外官吏俸米。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, salary rice for inner and outer officials was first added.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year a rice allowance was first added to the pay of all officials, court and local.

sentences.zh: 凡俸一十兩以下人員，依小吏例，每一兩給米一斗。

translations.literal: For all persons with salary below ten taels, following the petty-clerk precedent, for each tael one dou of rice was given.
translations.idiomatic: Officials paid less than ten taels of silver followed the junior-clerk rule: one dou of rice for each tael of salary.

sentences.zh: 十兩以上至二十五兩，每員給米一石。

translations.literal: From ten taels up to twenty-five, each person received one shi of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Those earning from ten to twenty-five taels received one shi of rice each.

sentences.zh: 余上之數，每俸一兩給米一升。

translations.literal: For amounts above that, for each tael of salary one sheng of rice was given.
translations.idiomatic: Above twenty-five taels, each additional tael of salary brought one sheng of rice.

sentences.zh: 無米，則驗其時直給價，雖貴每石不過二十兩。

translations.literal: Where there was no rice, the current price was verified and cash given; even if dear, per shi it did not exceed twenty taels.
translations.idiomatic: Where rice was unavailable, officials were paid in cash at the market rate, capped at twenty taels per shi even when grain was scarce.

sentences.zh: 上都、大同、隆興、甘肅等處，素非產米之地，每石權給中統鈔二十五兩，俸三錠以上者不給。

translations.literal: At Shangdu, Datong, Longxing, Gansu, and the like—places that were never rice-producing—per shi twenty-five taels of Zhongtong notes were provisionally given; those with salary of three ingots and above received none.
translations.idiomatic: In non-rice-growing regions such as Shangdu, Datong, Longxing, and Gansu, a substitute of twenty-five taels of Zhongtong paper money per shi was paid instead; officials whose salary reached three ingots or more received no rice allowance.

sentences.zh: 至大二年，詔隨朝官員及軍官等俸改給至元鈔，而罷其俸米。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhida, an edict ordered that salaries of officials attending court and military officers be changed to Zhiyuan notes, and their salary rice abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhida 2 (1309) court officials and military officers were paid entirely in Zhiyuan paper money, and the rice supplement was discontinued.

sentences.zh: 延祐七年，又命隨朝官吏俸以十分為率，給米三分。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yanyou, it was again ordered that court officials’ salaries, taking ten parts as the standard, receive rice at three parts.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanyou 7 (1320) court officials again received rice equal to thirty percent of their cash salary.

sentences.zh: 凡諸官員上任者不過初二日，罷任者已過初五日，給當月俸。

translations.literal: For all officials, if taking office no later than the second day, or leaving office after the fifth day, the salary of that month was given.
translations.idiomatic: An official who took up his post by the second day of the month, or who left after the fifth, received the full salary for that month.

sentences.zh: 各路官擅割官吏俸者罪之。

translations.literal: Circuit officials who on their own authority cut officials’ salaries were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit authorities who diverted or withheld subordinates’ salaries were subject to punishment.

sentences.zh: 諸職官病假百日之外，及因病求醫、親老告侍者，不給祿。

translations.literal: All officeholders beyond one hundred days of sick leave, and those seeking medical treatment because of illness or requesting leave to serve aged parents, received no salary.
translations.idiomatic: Officials on sick leave for more than one hundred days, those absent to seek medical care, or those granted leave to nurse elderly parents received no pay.

sentences.zh: 後官已至，而前官被差者，其俸兩給之。

translations.literal: When the successor had arrived but the predecessor had been dispatched on assignment, both received salary.
translations.idiomatic: If a successor had already arrived while the outgoing official was still on a temporary assignment, both men were paid.

sentences.zh: 隨朝官吏每月給俸，如告假事故，當官立限者全給，違限托故者追罰。

translations.literal: Court officials received monthly salary; if reporting leave for cause, those with limits set by the responsible official received full pay; those exceeding limits on pretext were pursued and penalized.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials were paid monthly; approved leave within the time set by one’s superior was paid in full, but extensions without good cause led to recovery of salary.

sentences.zh: 軍官差出者許借俸，歿於王事者借俸免征。

translations.literal: Military officers dispatched on assignment were permitted to borrow salary; those who died in the king’s service had borrowed salary exempted from collection.
translations.idiomatic: Officers on campaign might draw salary in advance; if they died in the line of duty, any advance was not recovered from their estate.

sentences.zh: 各投下保充路府州縣等官，其俸與王官等。

translations.literal: Officials of circuits, prefectures, districts, and counties installed by each appanage received salary equal to regular officials.
translations.idiomatic: Officials appointed to local posts by imperial appanage holders were paid on the same scale as regular government appointees.

sentences.zh: 職田之制，路府州縣官至元三年定之，按察司官十四年定之，江南行省及諸司官二十一年定之，其數減腹裏之半。

translations.literal: As for the system of official lands, circuit, prefecture, district, and county officials were fixed in Zhiyuan year 3; Surveillance Commission officials in year 14; Jiangnan Branch Secretariat and various office officials in year 21—the amounts were half those of the metropolitan core.
translations.idiomatic: Official land allotments for local and surveillance officials were set in Zhiyuan 3, 14, and 21 respectively; in the Jiangnan region the grants were half the size of those in the metropolitan provinces.

sentences.zh: 至武宗至大二年，外官有職田者，三品給祿米一百石，四品給六十石，五品五十石，六品四十五石，七品以下四十石；

translations.literal: By Wuzong’s Zhida year 2, outer officials with official lands: third rank received one hundred shi of salary rice, fourth rank sixty shi, fifth rank fifty shi, sixth rank forty-five shi, seventh rank and below forty shi;
translations.idiomatic: In Zhida 2 under Emperor Wuzong, local officials who held official land received rice supplements by rank: one hundred shi for third rank, sixty for fourth, fifty for fifth, forty-five for sixth, and forty for seventh rank and below;

sentences.zh: 俸鈔改支至元鈔，其田拘收入官。

translations.literal: salary notes were changed to payment in Zhiyuan notes, and their lands were seized and turned in to the state.
translations.idiomatic: their cash salaries were paid in Zhiyuan notes instead, and their official lands were confiscated to the government.

sentences.zh: 四年，又詔公田及俸皆復舊制。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an edict again restored public lands and salaries to the old system.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year official land and salary arrangements were restored to the previous system.

sentences.zh: 延祐三年，外官無職田者，量給粟麥。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yanyou, outer officials without official lands were given grain and wheat in measured amounts.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanyou 3 local officials who held no official land were granted measured allotments of grain and wheat.

sentences.zh: 凡交代官芒種已前去任者，其租後官收之，已後去任者前官分收。

translations.literal: For all transferring officials, if before Grain-in-Ear they had gone to their post, the rent was collected by the successor; if after leaving their post, the predecessor shared collection.
translations.idiomatic: When officials changed posts, rent from official land sown before Grain-in-Ear went to the incoming officer; if the outgoing officer left after that date, he shared the harvest rent.

sentences.zh: 後又以爭競者多，俾各驗其俸月以為多寡。

translations.literal: Later, because disputes were many, each was made to verify salary months to determine the amount.
translations.idiomatic: Because disputes over these shares became frequent, the division was later calculated according to how many months each man had actually held salary.

sentences.zh: 其大略如此。

translations.literal: The general outline was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the broad outline of the system.

sentences.zh: 今取其制之可考者，具列於後。

translations.literal: Now what can be verified of the system is fully listed below.
translations.idiomatic: What follows is a full listing of the regulations that can still be documented.

sentences.zh: 至元二十二年百官俸例，各品分上中下三等：

translations.literal: Salary precedents for the hundred offices in Zhiyuan year 22; each grade divided into upper, middle, and lower three grades:
translations.idiomatic: Salary scales fixed in Zhiyuan 22 (1285), with upper, middle, and lower rates for each rank:

sentences.zh: 從一品六錠五錠正二品四錠二十五兩四錠一十五兩從二品四錠三錠三十五兩三錠二十五兩正三品三錠二十五兩三錠一十五兩三錠從三品三錠

translations.literal: Secondary first rank: six ingots, five ingots; regular second rank: four ingots twenty-five taels, four ingots fifteen taels; secondary second rank: four ingots, three ingots thirty-five taels, three ingots twenty-five taels; regular third rank: three ingots twenty-five taels, three ingots fifteen taels, three ingots; secondary third rank: three ingots
translations.idiomatic: Secondary first rank—upper six ingots, middle five ingots; regular second rank—upper four ingots twenty-five taels, middle four ingots fifteen taels; secondary second rank—upper four ingots, middle three ingots thirty-five taels, lower three ingots twenty-five taels; regular third rank—upper three ingots twenty-five taels, middle three ingots fifteen taels, lower three ingots; secondary third rank—upper three ingots

sentences.zh: 二錠三十五兩二錠二十五兩正四品二錠二十五兩

translations.literal: two ingots thirty-five taels, two ingots twenty-five taels; regular fourth rank: two ingots twenty-five taels
translations.idiomatic: middle two ingots thirty-five taels, lower two ingots twenty-five taels; regular fourth rank—upper two ingots twenty-five taels

sentences.zh: 二錠一十五兩二錠從四品二錠一錠四十五兩一錠四十兩正五品一錠四十兩一錠三十兩從五品一錠三十兩一錠二十兩正六品一錠二十兩一錠一十五兩從六品一錠一十五兩一錠一十兩正七品一錠一十兩

translations.literal: two ingots fifteen taels, two ingots; secondary fourth rank: two ingots, one ingot forty-five taels, one ingot forty taels; regular fifth rank: one ingot forty taels, one ingot thirty taels; secondary fifth rank: one ingot thirty taels, one ingot twenty taels; regular sixth rank: one ingot twenty taels, one ingot fifteen taels; secondary sixth rank: one ingot fifteen taels, one ingot ten taels; regular seventh rank: one ingot ten taels
translations.idiomatic: middle two ingots fifteen taels, lower two ingots; secondary fourth rank—upper two ingots, middle one ingot forty-five taels, lower one ingot forty taels; regular fifth rank—upper one ingot forty taels, middle one ingot thirty taels; secondary fifth rank—upper one ingot thirty taels, middle one ingot twenty taels; regular sixth rank—upper one ingot twenty taels, middle one ingot fifteen taels; secondary sixth rank—upper one ingot fifteen taels, middle one ingot ten taels; regular seventh rank—upper one ingot ten taels

sentences.zh: 一錠五兩從七品一錠五兩一錠正八品一錠

translations.literal: one ingot five taels; secondary seventh rank: one ingot five taels, one ingot; regular eighth rank: one ingot
translations.idiomatic: middle one ingot five taels; secondary seventh rank—upper one ingot five taels, middle one ingot; regular eighth rank—upper one ingot

sentences.zh: 四十五兩從八品四十五兩四十兩正九品四十兩三十五兩從九品三十五兩內外官俸數：

translations.literal: forty-five taels; secondary eighth rank: forty-five taels, forty taels; regular ninth rank: forty taels, thirty-five taels; secondary ninth rank: thirty-five taels. Salaries of inner and outer officials:
translations.idiomatic: middle forty-five taels; secondary eighth rank—upper forty-five taels, middle forty taels; regular ninth rank—upper forty taels, middle thirty-five taels; secondary ninth rank—upper thirty-five taels. Detailed salaries of court and local officials:

sentences.zh: 太師府：太師，俸一百四十貫，米一十五石。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor’s Office: Grand Preceptor, salary one hundred forty guan, rice fifteen shi.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor’s Office: the Grand Preceptor received 140 guan in salary and fifteen shi of rice.

sentences.zh: 諮議、參軍，俸四十五貫，米四石五斗。

translations.literal: Counselor and Staff Adjutant, salary forty-five guan, rice four shi five dou.
translations.idiomatic: The Counselor and Staff Adjutant each received 45 guan and four shi five dou of rice.

sentences.zh: 長史，俸三十四貫六錢六分，米三石。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk, salary thirty-four guan six qian six fen, rice three shi.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Clerk received 34 guan 6 qian 6 fen and three shi of rice.

sentences.zh: 太傅、太保府同。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor and Grand Guardian offices the same.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Tutor’s and Grand Guardian’s offices followed the same scale.

sentences.zh: 監修國史、參軍、長史同。

translations.literal: Supervisor of the National History, Staff Adjutant, and Chief Clerk the same.
translations.idiomatic: The Supervisor of the National History and its Staff Adjutant and Chief Clerk were paid on the same terms.

sentences.zh: 中書省：右丞相，俸一百四十貫，米一十五石；

translations.literal: Secretariat: Right Chancellor, salary one hundred forty guan, rice fifteen shi;
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat: the Right Chancellor received 140 guan and fifteen shi of rice;

sentences.zh: 左丞相同。

translations.literal: Left Chancellor the same.
translations.idiomatic: the Left Chancellor the same.

sentences.zh: 平章政事，俸一百二十八貫六錢六分六厘，米一十二石。

translations.literal: Grand Councillor, salary one hundred twenty-eight guan six qian six fen six li, rice twelve shi.
translations.idiomatic: the Grand Councillor received 128 guan 6 qian 6 fen 6 li and twelve shi of rice.

sentences.zh: 右丞，俸一百一十八貫六錢六分六厘，米一十二石；

translations.literal: Right Vice Chancellor, salary one hundred eighteen guan six qian six fen six li, rice twelve shi;
translations.idiomatic: the Right Vice Chancellor, 118 guan 6 qian 6 fen 6 li and twelve shi of rice;

sentences.zh: 左丞同。

translations.literal: Left Vice Chancellor the same.
translations.idiomatic: the Left Vice Chancellor the same.

sentences.zh: 參知政事，俸九十五貫三錢三分三厘，米九石五斗。

translations.literal: Vice Grand Councillor, salary ninety-five guan three qian three fen three li, rice nine shi five dou.
translations.idiomatic: the Vice Grand Councillor, 95 guan 3 qian 3 fen 3 li and nine shi five dou of rice.

sentences.zh: 參議，俸五十九貫，米六石。

translations.literal: Participating Secretary, salary fifty-nine guan, rice six shi.
translations.idiomatic: the Participating Secretary, 59 guan and six shi of rice.

sentences.zh: 郎中，俸四十二貫，米四石五斗。

translations.literal: Director, salary forty-two guan, rice four shi five dou.
translations.idiomatic: the Director, 42 guan and four shi five dou of rice.

sentences.zh: 員外郎，俸三十四貫六錢六分六厘，米三石。

translations.literal: Vice Director, salary thirty-four guan six qian six fen six li, rice three shi.
translations.idiomatic: the Vice Director, 34 guan 6 qian 6 fen 6 li and three shi of rice.

sentences.zh: 都事，俸二十八貫，米三石。

translations.literal: Secretary-General, salary twenty-eight guan, rice three shi.
translations.idiomatic: the Secretary-General, 28 guan and three shi of rice.

sentences.zh: 承發管勾，俸二十五貫三錢三分三厘，米二石；

translations.literal: Dispatch Controller, salary twenty-five guan three qian three fen three li, rice two shi;
translations.idiomatic: the Dispatch Controller, 25 guan 3 qian 3 fen 3 li and two shi of rice;

sentences.zh: 照磨、省架閣庫管勾、回回架閣庫管勾並同。

translations.literal: Record Examiner, Provincial Archive Controller, and Muslim Archive Controller all the same.
translations.idiomatic: the Record Examiner, Provincial Archive Controller, and Muslim Archive Controller likewise.

sentences.zh: 檢校官，俸二十八貫，米三石五斗。

translations.literal: Inspector, salary twenty-eight guan, rice three shi five dou.
translations.idiomatic: the Inspector, 28 guan and three shi five dou of rice.

sentences.zh: 斷事官，內一十八員俸各八十二貫六錢六分六厘，米八石五斗；

translations.literal: Adjudication Officials: of these, eighteen posts each with salary eighty-two guan six qian six fen six li, rice eight shi five dou;
translations.idiomatic: Adjudication Officials: eighteen posts at 82 guan 6 qian 6 fen 6 li and eight shi five dou of rice each;

sentences.zh: 一十四員俸各五十九貫三錢三分三厘，米六石；

translations.literal: fourteen posts each with salary fifty-nine guan three qian three fen three li, rice six shi;
translations.idiomatic: fourteen posts at 59 guan 3 qian 3 fen 3 li and six shi of rice;

sentences.zh: 一員俸五十四貫六錢六分六厘，米五石五斗；

translations.literal: one post with salary fifty-four guan six qian six fen six li, rice five shi five dou;
translations.idiomatic: one post at 54 guan 6 qian 6 fen 6 li and five shi five dou;

sentences.zh: 常平義倉

translations.literal: Ever-Normal Granary and Charity Granary
translations.idiomatic: Ever-Normal and Charity Granaries

sentences.zh: 常平起於漢之耿壽昌，義倉起於唐之戴胄，皆救荒之良法也。

translations.literal: The ever-normal granary began with Geng Shouchang of Han; the charity granary with Dai Zhou of Tang—both excellent methods for famine relief.
translations.idiomatic: Ever-normal granaries trace back to Geng Shouchang in the Han, and charity granaries to Dai Zhou in the Tang; both were sound policies for warding off famine.

sentences.zh: 元立義倉於鄉社，又置常平於路府，使饑不損民，豐不傷農，粟直不低昂，而民無菜色，可謂善法漢、唐者矣。

translations.literal: The Yuan established charity granaries in village communities and also set up ever-normal granaries in circuits and prefectures, so that famine did not harm the people, abundance did not hurt the farmers, grain prices did not swing high or low, and the people showed no signs of hunger—one may say they improved well upon Han and Tang practice.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan placed charity granaries in rural communities and ever-normal granaries in circuits and prefectures, aiming to spare the people in lean years and the farmers in fat years, keep grain prices steady, and prevent hunger—an admirable revival of Han and Tang wisdom.

sentences.zh: 今考其制，常平倉世祖至元六年始立。

translations.literal: Examining the system now, the ever-normal granary was first established in Shizu’s Zhiyuan year 6.
translations.idiomatic: As for the institutions themselves, the ever-normal granary was first founded in Kublai’s sixth Zhiyuan year.

sentences.zh: 其法：豐年米賤，官為增價糴之；

translations.literal: The method: in years of abundance, when rice was cheap, the government raised the price and purchased grain.
translations.idiomatic: The rule was simple: in bumper years, when rice was cheap, officials bought it at an increased price.

sentences.zh: 歉年米貴，官為減價糶之。

translations.literal: In years of scarcity, when rice was dear, the government lowered the price and sold grain.
translations.idiomatic: In lean years, when rice was dear, they sold from the granary at a reduced price.

sentences.zh: 於是八年以和糴糧及諸河倉所撥糧貯焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon in year 8 grain from equitable purchase and grain allocated from various river granaries were stored there.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, grain from equitable-purchase programs and transfers from river granaries were deposited in these stores.

sentences.zh: 二十三年定鐵法，又以鐵課糴糧充焉。

translations.literal: In year 23 the iron levy was fixed, and grain purchased with iron tax revenue was also used to fill them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, after the iron tax was regularized, grain bought with iron-tax receipts was added as well.

sentences.zh: 義倉亦至元六年始立。

translations.literal: Charity granaries were also first established in Zhiyuan year 6.
translations.idiomatic: Charity granaries likewise began in Zhiyuan 6.

sentences.zh: 其法：社置一倉，以社長主之，豐年每親丁納粟五斗，驅丁二斗，無粟聽納雜色，歉年就給社民。

translations.literal: The method: each community set up one granary, headed by the community chief; in abundant years each adult male paid five dou of grain and each dependent male two dou; those without grain could pay in other goods; in scarce years grain was issued to community members.
translations.idiomatic: Each community maintained one granary under its chief; in good years every adult male contributed five dou and every dependent male two dou (or other goods in lieu of grain), and in famine years the stock was distributed among members.

sentences.zh: 於是二十一年新城縣水，二十九年東平等處饑，皆發義倉賑之。

translations.literal: Thereupon in year 21 Xincheng County suffered flooding; in year 29 Dongping and other places faced famine—charity granaries were opened in each case for relief.
translations.idiomatic: In practice, when Xincheng County flooded in year 21 and Dongping and elsewhere went hungry in year 29, charity granaries were opened to relieve the people.

sentences.zh: 皇慶二年，復申其令。

translations.literal: In Huangqing year 2 the order was reissued.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangqing 2 the regulations were proclaimed again.

sentences.zh: 然行之既久，名存而實廢，豈非有司之過與？

translations.literal: Yet after long implementation the name survived while the substance decayed—is this not the fault of the officials in charge?
translations.idiomatic: Yet in time the institutions survived in name only while their substance withered—surely a failure of those charged with enforcing them.

sentences.zh: 惠民藥局

translations.literal: Benefit-the-People Pharmacy
translations.idiomatic: Benefit-the-People Pharmacies

sentences.zh: 《周官》有醫師，掌醫之政令，凡邦有疾病疕瘍者造焉，則使醫分而治之，此民所以無夭折之患也。

translations.literal: The Offices of Zhou had Physicians, who held the government’s medical ordinances; whenever the state had persons ill with disease, sores, or ulcers they came to them, and physicians were sent to treat them by division—thus the people were spared the calamity of early death.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou describe royal physicians who governed medical policy: anyone in the realm afflicted with illness or sores was sent to them and treated by assigned specialists, sparing the people untimely death.

sentences.zh: 元立惠民藥局，官給鈔本，月營子錢，以備藥物，仍擇良醫主之，以療貧民，其深得《周官》設醫師之美意者與。

translations.literal: The Yuan established Benefit-the-People Pharmacies; the government supplied note capital, and each month interest was earned to stock medicines; able physicians were still chosen to direct them and treat the poor—did this not deeply capture the fine intent of the Zhou in appointing physicians?
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan founded Benefit-the-People Pharmacies, advancing paper-note capital whose monthly interest funded medicines, with skilled doctors appointed to treat the poor—a thoughtful echo of the Zhou royal physicians.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗九年，如於燕京等十路置局，以奉御田闊闊、太醫王璧、齊楫等為局官，給銀五百錠為規運之本。

translations.literal: At first, in Taizong year 9, bureaus were placed in ten circuits such as Yanjing; the eunuch Tian Kuoku, Imperial Physician Wang Bi, and Qi Ji were made bureau officers, and five hundred ingots of silver were granted as operating capital.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, in Ögedei’s ninth year, pharmacies were opened in ten circuits including Yanjing; the eunuch Tian Kuoku, Imperial Physician Wang Bi, and Qi Ji were appointed directors, with five hundred silver ingots as seed capital.

sentences.zh: 世祖中統二年，又命王祐開局。

translations.literal: In Shizu’s Zhongtong year 2, Wang You was again ordered to open a bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In Kublai’s second Zhongtong year, Wang You was again ordered to establish a pharmacy.

sentences.zh: 四年，復置局於上都，每中統鈔一百兩，收息錢一兩五錢。

translations.literal: In year 4 bureaus were re-established at Shangdu; for every one hundred liang of Zhongtong notes, one liang five qian of interest was collected.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year pharmacies were restored at Shangdu, collecting one liang five qian of interest per hundred liang of Zhongtong notes invested.

sentences.zh: 至元二十五年，以陷失官本，悉罷革之。

translations.literal: In Zhiyuan year 25, because official capital had been lost, all were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 25, after state capital was lost, the pharmacies were shut down entirely.

sentences.zh: 至成宗大德三年，又準舊例，於各路置焉。

translations.literal: In Chengzong’s Dade year 3 the old precedent was approved and bureaus were again placed in each circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chengzong, in Dade 3 the former practice was restored and pharmacies were set up again in every circuit.

sentences.zh: 凡局皆以各路正官提調，所設良醫，上路二名，下路府州各一名，其所給鈔本，亦驗民戶多寡以為等差。

translations.literal: Every bureau was supervised by the circuit’s chief regular official; able physicians were appointed—two on a superior route, one each on inferior routes, prefectures, and districts; note capital granted also followed graded differences according to the number of households.
translations.idiomatic: Each pharmacy fell under the circuit’s senior civil officer; skilled doctors were assigned—two on superior routes, one on inferior routes and at prefectures and districts—and note capital was scaled to local household counts.
