translations.literal: Market Purchase of Grain
translations.idiomatic: Government Grain Purchases

sentences.zh: 和糴自唐始，所以備邊庭軍需也，其弊至於害民者，蓋有之矣。

translations.literal: Equitable purchase began in the Tang to supply border garrisons; its abuses sometimes reached the point of harming the people—this indeed occurred.
translations.idiomatic: Equitable purchase (hedi) began in the Tang to provision frontier armies, though at times its abuses truly injured the populace.

sentences.zh: 元和糴之名有二，曰市糴糧，曰鹽折草，率皆增其直而市於民。

translations.literal: Under the Yuan the name of equitable purchase had two forms: “market-purchase grain” and “salt exchanged for fodder”—both generally raised prices and bought from the people.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan knew two kinds of state buying: market-purchase grain and salt-for-fodder exchange, both typically at premium prices paid to civilians.

sentences.zh: 於是邊庭之兵不乏食，京師之馬不乏芻，而民亦用以不困，其為法不亦善乎！

translations.literal: Thereupon border troops did not lack food, capital horses did not lack fodder, and the people were likewise not distressed—was the method not also good!
translations.idiomatic: Frontier armies stayed fed, capital stables stayed stocked with hay, and the people were not unduly burdened—a policy with much to commend it.

sentences.zh: 市糴糧之法，世祖中統二年，始以鈔一千二百錠，於上都、北京、西京等處糴三萬石。

translations.literal: As for the method of market-purchase grain: in Shizu’s Zhongtong year 2, 1,200 ingots of notes were first used to purchase 30,000 shi at Shangdu, Beijing, Xijing, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: Market-purchase grain began in Kublai’s second Zhongtong year, when 1,200 ingots bought 30,000 shi at Shangdu, Beijing, Xijing, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 四年，以解鹽引一萬五千道，和中陜西軍儲。

translations.literal: In year 4, 15,000 salt certificates from Jie Prefecture were used to purchase grain equitably for Shaanxi military stores.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, 15,000 Jie salt certificates procured grain for Shaanxi army depots through equitable purchase.

sentences.zh: 是年三月，又命紥馬剌丁糴糧，仍敕軍民官毋沮。

translations.literal: In the third month of that year Jamal al-Din was again ordered to purchase grain, with a decree that military and civil officials must not obstruct it.
translations.idiomatic: That March, Jamal al-Din was again tasked with grain purchases, and officials were forbidden to interfere.

sentences.zh: 五年，諭北京、西京等路市糴軍糧。

translations.literal: In year 5 Beijing, Xijing, and other circuits were instructed to market-purchase military grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Beijing, Xijing, and other routes were told to buy army grain on the market.

sentences.zh: 至元三年，以南京等處和糴四十萬石。

translations.literal: In Zhiyuan year 3, 400,000 shi were equitably purchased in Nanjing and other places.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 3, 400,000 shi were bought by equitable purchase in Nanjing and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 四年，命沔州等處中納官糧，續還其直。

translations.literal: In year 4 Mianzhou and other places were ordered to deliver official grain in advance, with payment to follow.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Mianzhou and other districts advanced official grain to the state, to be paid for afterward.

sentences.zh: 八年，驗各路糧粟價直，增十分之一，和糴三十九萬四千六百六十石。

translations.literal: In year 8, after verifying grain prices in each circuit and adding one-tenth, 394,660 shi were equitably purchased.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, local grain prices were checked, a ten-percent premium was added, and 394,660 shi were purchased.

sentences.zh: 十六年，以兩淮鹽引五萬道，募客旅中糧。

translations.literal: In year 16, 50,000 Liang-Huai salt certificates were used to recruit traveling merchants to advance grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, 50,000 Liang-Huai salt certificates enlisted traveling merchants to supply grain on credit.

sentences.zh: 十九年，以鈔三萬錠，市糴於隆興等處。

translations.literal: In year 19, 30,000 ingots of notes were used for market purchase in Longxing and other places.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, 30,000 ingots bought grain at market prices in Longxing and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 二十年，以鈔五千錠市於北京，六萬錠市於上都，二千錠市於應昌。

translations.literal: In year 20, 5,000 ingots bought grain at Beijing, 60,000 ingots at Shangdu, and 2,000 ingots at Yingchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, purchases ran to 5,000 ingots at Beijing, 60,000 at Shangdu, and 2,000 at Yingchang.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，以河間、山東、兩浙、兩淮鹽引，募諸人中糧。

translations.literal: In year 21 salt certificates from Hejian, Shandong, Liang-Zhe, and Liang-Huai were used to recruit people to advance grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, salt certificates from Hejian, Shandong, Liang-Zhe, and Liang-Huai drew merchants and locals to advance grain.

sentences.zh: 是年四月，以鈔四千錠，於應昌市糴。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of that year, 4,000 ingots were used for market purchase at Yingchang.
translations.idiomatic: That April, 4,000 ingots bought grain at Yingchang.

sentences.zh: 九月，發鹽引七萬道、鈔三萬錠，於上都和糴。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, 70,000 salt certificates and 30,000 ingots were sent for equitable purchase at Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: In September, 70,000 salt certificates and 30,000 ingots funded equitable purchase at Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，以鈔五萬錠，令木八剌沙和糴於上都。

translations.literal: In year 22, 50,000 ingots were issued for Mubalasha to conduct equitable purchase at Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, 50,000 ingots empowered Mubalasha to buy grain equitably at Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 是年二月，詔江南民田秋成，官為定例收糴，次年減價出糶。

translations.literal: In the second month of that year an edict ordered that after the autumn harvest of Jiangnan private fields, the government would purchase grain by fixed rule and sell it at reduced price the following year.
translations.idiomatic: That February, the court decreed that after the Jiangnan autumn harvest officials would buy peasant grain at set rates and release it at lower prices the next year.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，發鈔五千錠，市糴沙、凈、隆興軍糧。

translations.literal: In year 23, 5,000 ingots were issued to market-purchase army grain for Sha, Jing, and Longxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, 5,000 ingots bought army grain for Sha, Jing, and Longxing.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，官發鹽引，聽民中糧。

translations.literal: In year 24 the government issued salt certificates, allowing the people to advance grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, salt certificates were issued so civilians could advance grain to the state.

sentences.zh: 是年十二月，以揚州、杭州鹽引五十萬道，兌換民糧。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of that year, 500,000 Yangzhou and Hangzhou salt certificates were used to exchange for civilian grain.
translations.idiomatic: That December, 500,000 Yangzhou and Hangzhou salt certificates were redeemed for grain supplied by the people.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，和糴西京糧，其價每一十兩之上增一兩。

translations.literal: In year 27 grain was equitably purchased for Xijing, the price increased by one liang for every ten liang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year, Xijing grain was bought equitably with a one-liang premium added to every ten liang of price.

sentences.zh: 延祐三年，中糴和林糧二十三萬石。

translations.literal: In Yanyou year 3, 230,000 shi of grain were advanced for purchase at Karakorum (Helin).
translations.idiomatic: In Yanyou 3, merchants advanced 230,000 shi of grain for the Karakorum (Helin) stores.

sentences.zh: 五年、六年，又各和中二十萬石。

translations.literal: In years 5 and 6, 200,000 shi were again advanced in each year.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth and sixth years, another 200,000 shi were advanced annually.

sentences.zh: 鹽折草之法，成宗大德八年，定其則例。

translations.literal: As for the method of salt exchanged for fodder: in Chengzong’s Dade year 8 the regulations were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Salt-for-fodder exchange was codified in Chengzong’s eighth Dade year.

sentences.zh: 每年以河間鹽，令有司於五月預給京畿郡縣之民，至秋成，各驗鹽數輸草，以給京師秣馬之用。

translations.literal: Each year Hejian salt was ordered by local officials to be advanced in the fifth month to the people of metropolitan counties; at autumn harvest each household delivered fodder according to the salt received, to supply fodder for the capital’s horses.
translations.idiomatic: Every year Hejian salt was prepaid in the fifth month to households around the capital; after the autumn harvest they delivered fodder in proportion to the salt received, feeding the capital’s horses.

sentences.zh: 每鹽二斤，折草一束，重一十斤。

translations.literal: For every two jin of salt, one bundle of fodder weighing ten jin was exchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Two jin of salt bought one ten-jin bundle of fodder grass.

sentences.zh: 歲用草八百萬束，折鹽四萬引云。

translations.literal: Annual fodder use was eight million bundles, exchanging for 40,000 salt certificates—so recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Eight million bundles of fodder were needed yearly, equal to 40,000 salt certificates—or so the accounts state.

sentences.zh: 救荒之政，莫大於賑恤。

translations.literal: Among famine-relief policies, none is greater than relief and succor.
translations.idiomatic: Of all policies for relieving famine, none matters more than direct relief and care.

sentences.zh: 元賑恤之名有二：曰蠲免者，免其差稅，即《周官·大司徒》所謂薄征者也；

translations.literal: Yuan relief and succor had two names: “remission and exemption,” waiving corvée and taxes—the so-called “light levies” of the Grand Minister of Education in the Offices of Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan relief took two main forms: remission and exemption of levies and taxes—the “light taxation” described in the Zhou Grand Minister of Education;

sentences.zh: 曰賑貸者，給以米粟，即《周官·大司徒》所謂散利者也。

translations.literal: and “relief loans,” giving rice and grain—the so-called “dispersing benefits” of the Grand Minister of Education in the Offices of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: and relief loans of grain—the “dispersing benefits” likewise attributed to that Zhou minister.

sentences.zh: 然蠲免有以恩免者，有以災免者。

translations.literal: Yet remission and exemption included grace remissions and disaster remissions.
translations.idiomatic: Remissions themselves divided into benevolent amnesties and disaster waivers.

sentences.zh: 賑貸有以鰥寡孤獨而賑者，有以水旱疫癘而賑者，有以京師人物繁湊而每歲賑糶者。

translations.literal: Relief loans included relief for widowers, widows, orphans, and the solitary; relief for flood, drought, and epidemic; and relief sales each year for the capital’s dense population.
translations.idiomatic: Loans reached widowers and orphans, flood and plague victims, and—because the capital was so crowded—annual relief grain sales as well.

sentences.zh: 若夫納粟補官之令，亦救荒之一策也。

translations.literal: As for the order to donate grain for office, it too was one policy for relieving famine.
translations.idiomatic: The policy allowing grain donations in exchange for office was another famine measure.

sentences.zh: 其為制各不同，今並著於後，以見其仁厚愛民之意云。

translations.literal: Each institution differed; all are recorded below to show the court’s humane care for the people.
translations.idiomatic: The rules varied by case; they are set out below to show how generously the dynasty treated its subjects.

sentences.zh: 恩免之制：世祖中統元年，量減絲料、包銀分數。

translations.literal: On grace remissions: in Shizu’s Zhongtong year 1, silk quota and baoyin silver shares were reduced by measure.
translations.idiomatic: Grace remissions began in Kublai’s first Zhongtong year, when silk and baoyin quotas were scaled back.

sentences.zh: 二年，免西京、北京、燕京差發。

translations.literal: In year 2 corvée assignments were remitted for Xijing, Beijing, and Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, Xijing, Beijing, and Yanjing were freed from corvée levies.

sentences.zh: 是年二月，以真定、大名、河南、陜西、東平、益都、平陽等路，兵興之際，勞於轉輸，其差發減輕科取。

translations.literal: In the second month of that year, for Zhending, Daming, Henan, Shaanxi, Dongping, Yidu, Pingyang, and other circuits—because during the warfare transport labor had been heavy—corvée collections were reduced and lightened.
translations.idiomatic: That February, Zhending, Daming, Henan, Shaanxi, Dongping, Yidu, Pingyang, and other routes, exhausted by wartime transport, had their corvée levies lightened.

sentences.zh: 三年，北京等路以兵興供給繁重，免本歲絲料、包銀。

translations.literal: In year 3 Beijing and other circuits, because military supply burdens during the campaigns were heavy, that year’s silk quota and baoyin were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Beijing and similar routes, strained by wartime provisioning, were excused from that year’s silk and baoyin.

sentences.zh: 是年閏九月，以濟南路遭李鋋之亂，軍民皆饑，盡除差發。

translations.literal: In the intercalary ninth month of that year, because Jinan Circuit had suffered Li Tan’s rebellion and soldiers and civilians alike were starving, all corvée was completely remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary ninth month, Jinan—ravaged by Li Tan’s revolt and famine—was cleared of every corvée levy.

sentences.zh: 四年，以西涼民戶值渾都海、阿藍<角┦>兒之亂，人民流散，免差稅三年。

translations.literal: In year 4, because Xiliang households had suffered the turmoil of Hunduha and Alandar, with the people scattered, levies and taxes were remitted for three years.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Xiliang families uprooted by Hunduha and Alandar’s revolts received a three-year tax holiday.

sentences.zh: 至元元年，詔減明年包銀十分之三，全無業者十之七。

translations.literal: In Zhiyuan year 1 an edict reduced next year’s baoyin by three-tenths, and by seven-tenths for those with no livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 1, the court cut the coming year’s baoyin by thirty percent—or seventy percent for households without livelihood.

sentences.zh: 是年四月，逃戶復業者，免差稅三年。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of that year, fugitive households returning to farming were remitted levies and taxes for three years.
translations.idiomatic: That April, refugees who resumed farming enjoyed three years without levies or taxes.

sentences.zh: 三年，減中都包銀四分之一。

translations.literal: In year 3 the Central Capital’s baoyin was reduced by one-quarter.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, baoyin at the Central Capital was cut by a quarter.

sentences.zh: 十二年，蠲免包銀、絲線、俸鈔。

translations.literal: In year 12 baoyin, silk thread, and salary notes were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, baoyin, silk thread, and salary notes were waived.

sentences.zh: 是年八月，免河南路包銀三分之二，其餘路府亦免十之五。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of that year, Henan Circuit’s baoyin was remitted by two-thirds, and other circuits and prefectures by half.
translations.idiomatic: That August, Henan’s baoyin was cut by two-thirds and other routes and prefectures by half.

sentences.zh: 十九年，免諸路民戶明年包銀、俸鈔，及逃移戶差稅。

translations.literal: In year 19 baoyin and salary notes were remitted for all circuits next year, and levies on absconding households.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, every circuit was spared next year’s baoyin and salary notes, along with taxes on runaway households.

sentences.zh: 二十年，免大都、平灤民戶絲線、俸鈔。

translations.literal: In year 20 silk thread and salary notes were remitted for households in Dadu and Pingluan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, Dadu and Pingluan households were freed from silk thread and salary notes.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，除民間包銀三年，不使帶納俸鈔，盡免大都軍民地稅。

translations.literal: In year 22 civilian baoyin was abolished for three years, salary notes were no longer collected together with it, and Dadu military and civilian land taxes were entirely remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, the court abolished the household silver levy for three years, stopped bundling salary-note payments with it, and fully waived land taxes for troops and civilians in Dadu.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，免東京軍民絲線、包銀、俸鈔。

translations.literal: In year 24 silk thread, baoyin, and salary notes were remitted for military and civilian households in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, troops and civilians at the Eastern Capital were freed from silk thread, baoyin, and salary notes.

sentences.zh: 是年九月，除北京馬五百匹。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year, five hundred horses from Beijing were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: That September, the levy of five hundred horses from Beijing was waived.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，免遼陽、武平等處差發。

translations.literal: In year 25 corvée assignments in Liaoyang, Wuping, and other places were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year, corvée assignments in Liaoyang, Wuping, and elsewhere were cancelled.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，減河間、保定、平灤三路絲線之半，大都全免。

translations.literal: In year 27 silk thread of the Hejian, Baoding, and Pingluan circuits was reduced by half; Dadu was wholly remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year, silk thread levies in Hejian, Baoding, and Pingluan were cut by half, while Dadu was exempted entirely.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，詔免腹裏諸路包銀、俸鈔；

translations.literal: In year 28 an edict remitted baoyin and salary notes in all inner circuits;
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year, an edict waived baoyin and salary notes throughout the metropolitan region;

sentences.zh: 其大都、上都、隆興、平灤、大同、太原、河間、保定、武平、遼陽十路絲線並除之。

translations.literal: and silk thread in the ten circuits of Dadu, Shangdu, Longxing, Pingluan, Datong, Taiyuan, Hejian, Baoding, Wuping, and Liaoyang was also abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Silk thread in the ten circuits of Dadu, Shangdu, Longxing, Pingluan, Datong, Taiyuan, Hejian, Baoding, Wuping, and Liaoyang was abolished as well.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，免上都、隆興、平灤、保定、河間五路包銀、俸鈔。

translations.literal: In year 29 baoyin and salary notes in the five circuits of Shangdu, Longxing, Pingluan, Baoding, and Hejian were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, baoyin and salary notes were waived in Shangdu, Longxing, Pingluan, Baoding, and Hejian.

sentences.zh: 三十年，免大都差稅。

translations.literal: In year 30 corvée taxes in Dadu were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, corvée taxes in Dadu were remitted.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，成宗即位，詔免天下差稅有差。

translations.literal: In year 31, when Chengzong took the throne, an edict remitted corvée taxes throughout the realm in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year, upon Chengzong’s accession, the court ordered corvée taxes remitted empire-wide, each region according to its circumstances.

sentences.zh: 是年六月，免腹裏軍、站、匠、船、鹽、鐵等戶稅糧，及江南夏稅之半。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of that year, grain taxes of military, postal, artisan, shipping, salt, and iron households in the inner circuits were remitted, and half of the Jiangnan summer tax.
translations.idiomatic: That June, grain taxes for military, postal, artisan, shipping, salt, and iron households in the metropolitan region were waived, along with half the Jiangnan summer tax.

sentences.zh: 元貞元年，除大都民戶絲線、包銀、稅糧。

translations.literal: In Yuanzhen year 1 silk thread, baoyin, and grain taxes of Dadu civilian households were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanzhen 1, Dadu civilians were freed from silk thread, baoyin, and grain taxes.

sentences.zh: 大德元年，以改元免大都、上都、隆興民戶差稅三年。

translations.literal: In Dade year 1, on the change of reign title, corvée taxes of civilian households in Dadu, Shangdu, and Longxing were remitted for three years.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 1, the new reign brought a three-year waiver of corvée taxes for civilians in Dadu, Shangdu, and Longxing.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔免腹裏包銀、俸鈔，及江南夏稅十分之三。

translations.literal: In year 3 an edict remitted inner-circuit baoyin and salary notes, and three-tenths of the Jiangnan summer tax.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, an edict waived baoyin and salary notes in the metropolitan region and cut the Jiangnan summer tax by thirty percent.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔免上都、大都、隆興明年絲銀稅糧，其數亦如之，江南租稅減十分之一。

translations.literal: In year 4 an edict remitted next year’s silk, silver, and grain taxes in Shangdu, Dadu, and Longxing in the same amounts; Jiangnan rents and taxes were reduced by one-tenth.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Shangdu, Dadu, and Longxing were promised the same relief on next year’s silk, silver, and grain levies, while Jiangnan rents and taxes fell by ten percent.

sentences.zh: 九年，又下寬免之令，以恤大都、上都、隆興、腹裏、江淮之民。

translations.literal: In year 9 another order of lenient remission was issued to comfort the people of Dadu, Shangdu, Longxing, the inner circuits, and the Jiang-Huai region.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, the court again issued broad remissions to ease the burden on Dadu, Shangdu, Longxing, the metropolitan region, and the Jiang-Huai provinces.

sentences.zh: 十年，逃移民戶復業者，免差稅三年。

translations.literal: In year 10 fugitive households returning to their occupations were remitted corvée taxes for three years.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, refugees who resumed farming enjoyed three years without corvée taxes.

sentences.zh: 十一年，武宗即位，詔免內外郡縣差稅有差。

translations.literal: In year 11, when Wuzong took the throne, an edict remitted corvée taxes inside and outside the commanderies and counties in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, upon Wuzong’s accession, corvée taxes were remitted at differing rates across inner and outer prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 至大二年，上尊號，詔免腹裏、江淮差稅。

translations.literal: In Zhide year 2, upon the bestowal of a honorific title, an edict remitted corvée taxes in the inner circuits and the Jiang-Huai region.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide 2, when the emperor received a honorific title, corvée taxes in the metropolitan region and Jiang-Huai were waived.

sentences.zh: 三年，又免大都、上都、中都秋稅，及民間差稅之負欠者。

translations.literal: In year 3 autumn taxes in Dadu, Shangdu, and Zhongdu were again remitted, and outstanding corvée debts of the populace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, autumn taxes in Dadu, Shangdu, and Zhongdu were waived again, along with unpaid corvée arrears.

sentences.zh: 四年，免腹裏包銀及江南夏稅十分之三。

translations.literal: In year 4 inner-circuit baoyin and three-tenths of the Jiangnan summer tax were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, baoyin in the metropolitan region and thirty percent of the Jiangnan summer tax were remitted.

sentences.zh: 是年四月，免大都、上都、中都差稅三年。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of that year, corvée taxes in Dadu, Shangdu, and Zhongdu were remitted for three years.
translations.idiomatic: That April, Dadu, Shangdu, and Zhongdu received a three-year corvée tax holiday.

sentences.zh: 延祐元年，以改元免大都、上都差稅二年，其餘被災經賑者免一年，流民復業者免差稅三年。

translations.literal: In Yanyou year 1, on the change of reign title, corvée taxes in Dadu and Shangdu were remitted for two years; elsewhere disaster-stricken and relief-aided places for one year; returning vagrants for three years.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanyou 1, the new reign brought two years’ relief in Dadu and Shangdu, one year for disaster-hit and relief districts, and three years for vagrants who resumed settlement.

sentences.zh: 二年，免各路差稅、絲料。

translations.literal: In year 2 corvée taxes and silk levies on all circuits were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, corvée taxes and silk levies were waived on every circuit.

sentences.zh: 七年，免腹裏絲綿十分之五，外郡十分之三，江淮夏稅所免之數，與外郡絲綿同，民間逋欠差稅並除之。

translations.literal: In year 7 five-tenths of inner-circuit silk floss were remitted, three-tenths in outer commanderies; the Jiang-Huai summer tax remission matched the outer silk floss rate, and outstanding corvée arrears were also abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, silk floss levies in the metropolitan region were cut by half and in outer prefectures by thirty percent; Jiang-Huai summer tax relief matched the outer silk rate, and all unpaid corvée debts were cancelled.

sentences.zh: 是年，免丁地稅糧、包銀、絲料各有差。

translations.literal: In that year, ding land grain taxes, baoyin, and silk levies were remitted in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: That year, ding land grain taxes, baoyin, and silk levies were waived to differing extents.

sentences.zh: 至治二年，寬恤軍民站戶。

translations.literal: In Zhizhi year 2 military and civilian postal households were given lenient relief.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizhi 2, the court extended relief to military and civilian postal households.

sentences.zh: 三年，免臨清萬戶府軍民船戶差稅三年，福建蜑戶差稅一年。

translations.literal: In year 3 corvée taxes of military, civilian, and shipping households in the Linqing Wanhu prefecture were remitted for three years, and Fujian boat-dweller households for one year.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Linqing Wanhu military, civilian, and shipping households received three years’ corvée relief, and Fujian boat-dwellers one year.

sentences.zh: 泰定三年，罷江淮以南包銀。

translations.literal: In Taiding year 3 baoyin south of the Jiang-Huai was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiding 3, the household silver levy south of the Jiang-Huai was abolished.

sentences.zh: 天歷元年，免諸路差稅、絲料有差，及海北鹽課三年。

translations.literal: In Tianli year 1 corvée taxes and silk levies on all circuits were remitted in varying degrees, and the Haibei salt levy for three years.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianli 1, corvée taxes and silk levies were waived circuit by circuit, and the Haibei salt levy for three years.

sentences.zh: 二年，免達達軍站之貧乏者及各路差稅有差。

translations.literal: In year 2 impoverished Mongol military postal households and corvée taxes on all circuits were remitted in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, poor Mongol postal troops and corvée taxes on every circuit were relieved to differing extents.

sentences.zh: 是年十月，免人民逋欠官錢，及奉元商稅，各處竈戶雜役。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year, outstanding government debts of the people, Fengyuan commercial taxes, and miscellaneous corvée of saltern households everywhere were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: That October, the court cancelled private arrears to the state, Fengyuan commercial taxes, and miscellaneous corvée for saltern households.

sentences.zh: 至順元年，以改元免諸路差稅有差，減方物之貢，免河南府、懷慶路門攤、海北鹽課，存恤紅城兒屯田軍三年。

translations.literal: In Zhishun year 1, on the change of reign title, corvée taxes on all circuits were remitted in varying degrees; tribute of local products was reduced; Henan prefecture and Huaiqing circuit stall levies and Haibei salt levies were remitted; Hongcheng’er garrison troops were sustained for three years.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhishun 1, the new reign brought graded corvée relief, reduced local tribute, waived stall levies in Henan and Huaiqing and Haibei salt taxes, and three years’ support for Hongcheng’er garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 災免之制：世祖中統元年，以各處被災，驗實減免科差。

translations.literal: Regulations on disaster remissions: In Zhongtong year 1 of Shizu, because various places suffered disaster, upon verification corvée levies were reduced and remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Disaster remissions: In Shizu’s first Zhongtong year, stricken districts had their corvée levies cut after on-site verification.

sentences.zh: 三年，以蠻寇攻掠，免三叉沽竈戶一百六十五戶其年絲料、包銀。

translations.literal: In year 3, because of barbarian raiders, the year’s silk levy and baoyin of 165 saltern households at Sanchagou were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, barbarian raids won a full waiver of that year’s silk and baoyin for 165 saltern households at Sanchagou.

sentences.zh: 四年，以秋旱霜災，減大名等路稅糧。

translations.literal: In year 4, because of autumn drought and frost disaster, grain taxes in Daming and other circuits were reduced.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, autumn drought and frost damage brought reductions in grain taxes across Daming and neighboring circuits.

sentences.zh: 至元三年，以東平等處蠶災，減其絲料。

translations.literal: In Zhiyuan year 3, because of silkworm disaster in Dongping and other places, their silk levies were reduced.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 3, silkworm disasters in Dongping and elsewhere prompted cuts in silk levies.

sentences.zh: 五年，以益都等路禾損，蠲其差稅。

translations.literal: In year 5, because of crop damage in Yidu and other circuits, their corvée taxes were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, crop losses in Yidu and other circuits earned full corvée remissions.

sentences.zh: 六年，以濟南、益都、懷孟、德州、淄萊、博州、曹州、真定、順德、河間、濟州、東平、恩州、南京等處桑蠶災傷，量免絲料。

translations.literal: In year 6, because of mulberry and silkworm disaster in Jinan, Yidu, Huaimeng, Dezhou, Zilai, Bozhou, Caozhou, Zhending, Shunde, Hejian, Jizhou, Dongping, Enzhou, Nanjing, and other places, silk levies were remitted as assessed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, mulberry and silkworm damage across Jinan, Yidu, Huaimeng, and a dozen other prefectures brought proportional silk levy relief.

sentences.zh: 七年，南京、河南蝗旱，減差徭十分之六。

translations.literal: In year 7, because of locusts and drought in Nanjing and Henan, corvée and labor levies were reduced by six-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, locusts and drought in Nanjing and Henan cut corvée and labor levies by sixty percent.

sentences.zh: 十九年，減京師民戶科差之半。

translations.literal: In year 19 corvée levies of capital civilian households were reduced by half.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, corvée levies on capital households were halved.

sentences.zh: 二十年，以水旱相仍，免江南稅糧十分之二。

translations.literal: In year 20, because flood and drought followed one upon another, two-tenths of Jiangnan grain taxes were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, successive floods and droughts brought a twenty-percent cut in Jiangnan grain taxes.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，免北京饑民差稅。

translations.literal: In year 24 corvée taxes of famine-stricken people in Beijing were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, corvée taxes for famine victims in Beijing were waived.

sentences.zh: 是年，揚州及浙西水，其地稅在揚州者全免，浙西減二分。

translations.literal: In that year Yangzhou and western Zhejiang suffered flood; land taxes registered in Yangzhou were wholly remitted, in western Zhejiang reduced by two-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: That year’s floods hit Yangzhou and western Zhejiang: Yangzhou land taxes were cancelled entirely, western Zhejiang’s cut by twenty percent.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，南安等處被寇兵者，稅糧免征。

translations.literal: In year 25, where Nan’an and other places suffered bandit armies, grain taxes were not levied.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year, districts ravaged by bandit armies such as Nan’an owed no grain taxes.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，紹興路水，免地稅十之三。

translations.literal: In year 26 Shaoxing circuit suffered flood; land taxes were remitted by three-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, flooding in Shaoxing circuit brought a thirty-percent land tax remission.

sentences.zh: 是年六月，以禾稼不收，免遼陽差稅。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of that year, because crops were not harvested, corvée taxes in Liaoyang were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: That June, failed harvests won a corvée tax holiday for Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，大都、遼陽被災，免其包銀、俸鈔。

translations.literal: In year 27, where Dadu and Liaoyang suffered disaster, baoyin and salary notes were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year, disaster-hit Dadu and Liaoyang were freed from baoyin and salary notes.

sentences.zh: 是年六月，以霖雨免河間等路絲料之半。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of that year, because of heavy rains, half of silk levies in Hejian and other circuits were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: That June, prolonged rains halved silk levies in Hejian and neighboring circuits.

sentences.zh: 十月，以興、松二州霜，免其地稅。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, because of frost in Xing and Song prefectures, their land taxes were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, frost damage in Xing and Song prefectures brought full land tax remissions.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，遼陽被災者，稅糧皆免征，其餘量征其半。

translations.literal: In year 28, where Liaoyang suffered disaster, grain taxes were not levied; elsewhere half was levied as assessed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year, disaster districts in Liaoyang owed no grain taxes; elsewhere collections were cut to half as assessed.

sentences.zh: 是年五月，以太原去歲不登，杭州被水，其太原丁地稅糧、杭州地稅並除之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of that year, because Taiyuan had failed to harvest the previous year and Hangzhou suffered flood, Taiyuan ding land grain taxes and Hangzhou land taxes were both abolished.
translations.idiomatic: That May, last year’s crop failure in Taiyuan and flooding in Hangzhou won abolition of Taiyuan ding land taxes and Hangzhou land taxes.

sentences.zh: 九月，又免州路所負歲糧。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, annual grain debts borne by prefectures and circuits were again remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In September, annual grain arrears owed by prefectures and circuits were cancelled as well.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，以北京地震，量減歲課。

translations.literal: In year 29, because of earthquake in Beijing, annual levies were reduced as assessed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, Beijing’s earthquake prompted proportional cuts in annual levies.

sentences.zh: 是年，以大都去歲不登，流移者眾，免其稅糧及包銀、俸鈔。

translations.literal: In that year, because Dadu had failed to harvest the previous year and many had drifted away, grain taxes and baoyin and salary notes were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: That year, Dadu’s poor harvest and mass displacement brought remission of grain taxes, baoyin, and salary notes.

sentences.zh: 元貞元年，以供給繁重及水傷禾稼，免咸平府邊民差稅。

translations.literal: In Yuanzhen year 1, because supply burdens were heavy and crops were damaged by water, corvée taxes of frontier people in Xianping prefecture were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanzhen 1, heavy supply demands and flood-damaged crops won corvée relief for Xianping’s frontier population.

sentences.zh: 大德三年，以旱蝗，除揚州、淮安兩路稅糧。

translations.literal: In Dade year 3, because of drought and locusts, grain taxes in Yangzhou and Huai’an circuits were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 3, drought and locusts brought abolition of grain taxes in Yangzhou and Huai’an.

sentences.zh: 五年，各路被災重者，其差稅並除之。

translations.literal: In year 5, where circuits suffered severe disaster, corvée taxes were also abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, circuits hit hardest by disaster were freed from corvée taxes altogether.

sentences.zh: 六年，免大都、平灤差稅。

translations.literal: In year 6 corvée taxes in Dadu and Pingluan were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, corvée taxes in Dadu and Pingluan were waived.

sentences.zh: 七年，以內郡饑，荊湖、川蜀供給軍餉，其差稅減免各有差。

translations.literal: In year 7, because the inner commanderies suffered famine and Jing-Hu and Sichuan supplied military provisions, corvée tax reductions were applied in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, famine in the heartland and military supply demands from Jing-Hu and Sichuan brought graded corvée relief.

sentences.zh: 八年，以平陽、太原地震，免差稅三年。

translations.literal: In year 8, because of earthquake in Pingyang and Taiyuan, corvée taxes were remitted for three years.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, earthquakes in Pingyang and Taiyuan earned three years without corvée taxes.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，以江南、江北水旱民饑，其科差、夏稅並免之。

translations.literal: In Zhide year 1, because of flood, drought, and famine in Jiangnan and Jiangbei, corvée levies and summer taxes were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide 1, flood, drought, and famine in Jiangnan and Jiangbei brought full remission of corvée levies and summer taxes.

sentences.zh: 二年，以腹裏、江淮被災，其科差、夏稅亦並免之。

translations.literal: In year 2, because the inner circuits and Jiang-Huai suffered disaster, corvée levies and summer taxes were also remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, disaster in the metropolitan region and Jiang-Huai likewise cancelled corvée levies and summer taxes.

sentences.zh: 皇慶二年，免益都饑民貸糧。

translations.literal: In Huangqing year 2 relief grain loans to famine victims in Yidu were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangqing 2, the court forgave relief grain loans to Yidu’s famine victims.

sentences.zh: 延祐二年，河南、歸德、南陽、徐、邳、陳、蔡、許州、荊門、襄陽等處水，三年，肅州等處連歲被災，皆免其民戶稅糧。

translations.literal: In Yanyou year 2 flood in Henan, Guide, Nanyang, Xu, Pi, Chen, Cai, Xuzhou, Jingmen, Xiangyang, and other places; in year 3 Su prefecture and other places suffered disaster year after year—all civilian grain taxes were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanyou 2, floods across Henan, Guide, Nanyang, and many other prefectures; in year 3, Su prefecture and others hit by successive disasters—all owed no civilian grain taxes.

sentences.zh: 天歷元年，陜西霜旱，免其科差一年；

translations.literal: In Tianli year 1, frost and drought in Shaanxi—corvée levies were remitted for one year;
translations.idiomatic: In Tianli 1, frost and drought in Shaanxi brought a one-year corvée holiday;

sentences.zh: 鹽官州海潮，免其秋糧夏稅。

translations.literal: sea tide at Yanguan prefecture—autumn grain and summer taxes were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: a sea surge at Yanguan prefecture won remission of autumn grain and summer taxes.

sentences.zh: 是年十二月，詔經寇盜剽掠州縣，免差稅一年。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of that year, an edict remitted corvée taxes for one year in prefectures and counties that had suffered bandit plunder.
translations.idiomatic: That December, an edict granted one year’s corvée relief to districts ravaged by bandit raids.

sentences.zh: 二年，以關陜旱，免差稅三年。

translations.literal: In year 2, because of drought in Guan-Shaan, corvée taxes were remitted for three years.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, drought in Guan-Shaan brought three years without corvée taxes.

sentences.zh: 至順元年，以河南、懷慶旱，其門攤課程及逋欠差稅皆免征。

translations.literal: In Zhishun year 1, because of drought in Henan and Huaiqing, stall levies and outstanding corvée taxes were not levied.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhishun 1, drought in Henan and Huaiqing cancelled stall levies and all unpaid corvée arrears.

sentences.zh: 鰥寡孤獨賑貸之制：世祖中統元年，首詔天下，鰥寡孤獨廢疾不能自存之人，天民之無告者也，命所在官司，以糧贍之。

translations.literal: Regulations on relief lending for widowers, orphans, and the solitary: In Zhongtong year 1 of Shizu, the first edict to the realm declared that widowers, orphans, the solitary, and the disabled who could not support themselves are Heaven’s people without recourse; local offices were ordered to sustain them with grain.
translations.idiomatic: Relief for widowers, orphans, and the destitute: In Shizu’s first Zhongtong year, the court’s inaugural edict declared that those who could not fend for themselves—widowers, orphans, the solitary, and the disabled—were Heaven’s forsaken; every local office must feed them from the public granary.

sentences.zh: 至元元年，又詔病者給藥，貧者給糧。

translations.literal: In Zhiyuan year 1, another edict ordered medicine for the sick and grain for the poor.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 1, a further edict promised medicine to the sick and grain to the poor.

sentences.zh: 八年，令各路設濟眾院以居處之，於糧之外，復給以薪。

translations.literal: In year 8 all circuits were ordered to establish Jizhong courtyards for their residence; beyond grain, fuel was also given.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, every circuit was to open a Jizhong courtyard for lodging, with fuel supplied on top of grain rations.

sentences.zh: 十年，以官吏破除入己，凡糧薪並敕於公廳給散。

translations.literal: In year 10, because officials had diverted supplies for themselves, all grain and fuel were ordered distributed at the public hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, after officials had pocketed relief supplies, grain and fuel had to be issued openly at the government hall.

sentences.zh: 十九年，各路立養濟院一所，仍委憲司點治。

translations.literal: In year 19 each circuit established one Yangji courtyard, still placed under surveillance commission inspection.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, each circuit founded a Yangji relief house, still subject to inspection by the surveillance commission.

sentences.zh: 二十年，給京師南城孤老衣糧房舍。

translations.literal: In year 20 clothing, grain, and housing were given to solitary elderly in the southern city of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, the capital’s southern city supplied clothing, grain, and shelter to solitary elders.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，給寡婦冬夏衣。

translations.literal: In year 28 winter and summer clothing was given to widows.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year, widows received winter and summer clothing.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，給貧子柴薪，日五斤。

translations.literal: In year 29 fuelwood was given to poor children, five jin per day.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, poor children received five jin of fuelwood daily.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，特賜米絹。

translations.literal: In year 31 rice and silk were specially bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year, the court made a special grant of rice and silk.

sentences.zh: 元貞二年，詔各處孤老，凡遇寬恩，人給布帛各一。

translations.literal: In Yuanzhen year 2 an edict ordered that wherever solitary elderly encountered lenient grace, each person was given one piece of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanzhen 2, an edict promised every registered solitary elder one bolt of cloth whenever the court proclaimed general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 大德三年，詔遇天壽節，人給中統鈔二貫，永為定例。

translations.literal: In Dade year 3 an edict ordered that on the Heavenly Longevity festival each person was given two guan of Zhongtong notes, permanently as a fixed rule.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 3, the Heavenly Longevity festival became a fixed occasion to give each recipient two guan of Zhongtong paper money.

sentences.zh: 六年，給死者棺木錢。

translations.literal: In year 6 money for coffin wood was given to the dead.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, the state paid for coffin wood for the deceased poor.

sentences.zh: 水旱疫癘賑貸之制：中統元年，平陽旱，遣使賑之。

translations.literal: Regulations on relief lending for flood, drought, and epidemic: In Zhongtong year 1, Pingyang suffered drought; envoys were dispatched to give relief.
translations.idiomatic: Flood, drought, and epidemic relief: In Zhongtong 1, drought in Pingyang brought imperial envoys with relief grain.

sentences.zh: 二年，遷曳捏即地貧民就食河南、平陽、太原。

translations.literal: In year 2 poor people of the Yienie’er land were relocated to find food in Henan, Pingyang, and Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, poor people from the Yienie’er region were resettled to subsist in Henan, Pingyang, and Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 三年，濟南饑，以糧三萬石賑之。

translations.literal: In year 3 Jinan suffered famine; thirty thousand shi of grain were used to give relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, famine in Jinan was met with thirty thousand shi of relief grain.

sentences.zh: 是年七月，以課銀一百五十錠濟甘州貧民。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of that year, 150 ingots of tax silver were used to aid poor people in Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That July, 150 ingots of tax silver went to Ganzhou’s poor.

sentences.zh: 四年，以錢糧幣帛賑東平濟河貧民，鈔四千錠賑諸王只必帖木兒部貧民。

translations.literal: In year 4 money, grain, and cloth were used to give relief to poor people along the Ji River in Dongping; four thousand ingots of notes gave relief to poor people in Prince Zhibi Temür’s domain.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, cash, grain, and cloth relieved Dongping’s Ji River poor, while four thousand ingots of notes aided the poor in Prince Zhibi Temür’s domain.

sentences.zh: 至元二年，以鈔百錠賑闊闊出所部軍。

translations.literal: In Zhiyuan year 2, one hundred ingots of notes gave relief to troops under Kuokuochu.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 2, one hundred ingots of notes relieved troops under Kuokuochu.

sentences.zh: 五年，益都民饑，驗口賑之。

translations.literal: In year 5 the people of Yidu suffered famine; relief was given per registered mouth.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, famine in Yidu brought relief apportioned by household headcount.

sentences.zh: 六年，東平、河間一十五處饑，亦驗口賑之。

translations.literal: In year 6 fifteen places including Dongping and Hejian suffered famine; relief was also given per registered mouth.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, fifteen districts including Dongping and Hejian received the same per-capita relief.

sentences.zh: 八年，以糧賑西京路急遞鋪兵卒。

translations.literal: In year 8 grain gave relief to express-relay post soldiers in the Western Capital circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, grain relief reached express-relay soldiers on the Western Capital circuit.

sentences.zh: 十二年，濮州等處饑，貸糧五千石。

translations.literal: In year 12 Puzhou and other places suffered famine; five thousand shi of grain were lent.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, famine in Puzhou and elsewhere was met with five thousand shi of loaned grain.

sentences.zh: 十六年，以江南所運糯米不堪用者賑貧民。

translations.literal: In year 16 glutinous rice transported from Jiangnan unfit for use was used to give relief to poor people.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, substandard Jiangnan glutinous rice in transit was distributed to the poor.

sentences.zh: 十九年，真定饑，賑糧兩月。

translations.literal: In year 19 Zhending suffered famine; relief grain for two months.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, Zhending’s famine brought two months of relief grain.

sentences.zh: 二十年，以帛千匹、鈔三百錠，賑水達達地貧民。

translations.literal: In year 20 one thousand bolts of cloth and three hundred ingots of notes gave relief to poor people in the Shuidada land.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, one thousand bolts of cloth and three hundred ingots of notes aided the Shuidada poor.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，大都屬郡六處饑，賑糧三月。

translations.literal: In year 23 six subordinate commanderies of the capital suffered famine; relief grain for three months.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, famine in six capital sub-prefectures brought three months of relief grain.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，斡端民饑，賑鈔萬錠。

translations.literal: In year 24 the people of Woduan suffered famine; ten thousand ingots of notes gave relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, famine in Woduan was met with ten thousand ingots of relief notes.

sentences.zh: 是年四月，以陳米給貧民。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of that year, aged grain was given to poor people.
translations.idiomatic: That April, stale grain from the granaries went to the poor.

sentences.zh: 七月，以糧給諸王阿只吉部貧民，大口二斗，小口一斗。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, grain was given to poor people in Prince Azhi’s domain: two dou for adults, one dou for children.
translations.idiomatic: In July, Prince Azhi’s poor received grain rations—two dou for adults, one for children.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，京兆旱，以糧三萬石賑之。

translations.literal: In year 26 Jingzhao suffered drought; thirty thousand shi of grain gave relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, drought in Jingzhao was answered with thirty thousand shi of relief grain.

sentences.zh: 是年，又賑左右翼屯田蠻軍及月兒魯部貧民糧，各三月。

translations.literal: That year, again grain was given in relief to the left and right wing garrison-field Man troops and to poor people of the Yue'erlu tribe, each for three months.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, left- and right-wing garrison Man troops and the poor of Yue'erlu's followers each received three months' grain relief.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，大都民饑，減直糶糧五萬石。

translations.literal: Year twenty-seven, Great Capital people suffered famine; reduced-price relief-sale grain fifty thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year, famine in the Great Capital was met with fifty thousand shi of grain sold at reduced price for relief.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，以去歲隕霜害稼，賑宿衛士怯憐口糧二月，以饑賑徽州、溧陽等路民糧三月。

translations.literal: Year twenty-eight, because last year's sky-falling frost harmed the crops, relief grain was given to imperial guard qielian dependents for two months; because of famine relief grain was given to people of Huizhou, Liyang, and other circuits for three months.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year, frost damage to the previous harvest brought two months' grain to imperial guard dependents and three months' relief to the people of Huizhou, Liyang, and neighboring circuits.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，復賑宿衛士怯憐口糧三月。

translations.literal: Year thirty-one, again relief grain was given to imperial guard qielian dependents for three months.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year, imperial guard dependents again received three months' relief grain.

sentences.zh: 元貞元年，諸王阿難答部民饑，賑糧二萬石。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen year one, Prince Ananda's fief people suffered famine; relief grain twenty thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yuanzhen, famine among Prince Ananda's people was answered with twenty thousand shi of relief grain.

sentences.zh: 是年六月，以糧一千三百石賑隆興府饑民，二千石賑千戶滅禿等軍。

translations.literal: That year, sixth month: with grain one thousand three hundred shi relief was given to Longxing prefecture famine people; two thousand shi relief was given to chiliarch Mietu and other troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of that year, Longxing's famine victims received 1,300 shi of grain and Mietu's chiliarchy and allied units 2,000 shi.

sentences.zh: 七月，以遼陽民饑，賑糧二月。

translations.literal: Seventh month, because Liaoyang people suffered famine, relief grain for two months.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, two months' relief grain went to famine-stricken Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 大德元年，以饑賑遼陽、水達達等戶糧五千石，公主囊加真位糧二千石。

translations.literal: Dade year one, because of famine relief grain was given to Liaoyang, Shuidada, and other households five thousand shi; Princess Nangiazhen's establishment grain two thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dade, famine relief brought 5,000 shi to Liaoyang and Shuidada households and 2,000 shi to Princess Nangiazhen's establishment.

sentences.zh: 是年，臨江、揚州等路亦饑，賑糧有差；

translations.literal: That year, Linjiang, Yangzhou, and other circuits also suffered famine; relief grain was apportioned by grade;
translations.idiomatic: That year Linjiang, Yangzhou, and other circuits also went hungry, and relief grain was allotted in graded amounts;

sentences.zh: 腹裏並江南災傷之地賑糧三月。

translations.literal: the interior provinces and Jiangnan disaster-stricken places received relief grain for three months.
translations.idiomatic: while the heartland and Jiangnan disaster zones each received three months' grain.

sentences.zh: 二年，賑龍興、臨江兩路饑民，又賑金復州屯田軍糧二月。

translations.literal: Year two, famine people of Longxing and Linjiang two circuits were given relief; also relief grain was given to Jinfu prefecture garrison-field troops for two months.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, Longxing and Linjiang received famine relief, and Jinfu's garrison troops two months' grain.

sentences.zh: 四年，鄂州等處民饑，發湖廣省糧十萬石賑之。

translations.literal: Year four, Ezhou and other places' people suffered famine; Huguang province grain one hundred thousand shi was issued to give them relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, famine in Ezhou and elsewhere was met with one hundred thousand shi from Huguang province.

sentences.zh: 七年，以鈔萬錠賑歸德饑民。

translations.literal: Year seven, with paper notes ten thousand ingots famine people of Guide were given relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Guide's famine victims received relief paid in ten thousand ingots of paper money.

sentences.zh: 九年，澧陽縣火，賑糧二月。

translations.literal: Year nine, Liyang county suffered fire; relief grain for two months.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, a fire at Liyang county brought two months' relief grain.

sentences.zh: 十一年，以饑賑安州高陽等縣糧五千石，漷州谷一萬石，奉符等處鈔二千錠，兩浙、江東等處鈔三萬餘錠、糧二十萬餘石。

translations.literal: Year eleven, because of famine: Anzhou Gaoyang and other counties grain five thousand shi, Huozhou grain ten thousand shi, Fengfu and other places notes two thousand ingots, Liangzhe and Jiangdong and other places notes thirty thousand-odd ingots and grain two hundred thousand-odd shi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of famine, Gaoyang in Anzhou and other counties received 5,000 shi, Huozhou 10,000 shi of grain, Fengfu and elsewhere 2,000 ingots of notes, and Liangzhe and Jiangdong more than 30,000 ingots and 200,000 shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 又勸率富戶賑糶糧一百四十餘萬石，凡施米者，驗其數之多寡，而授以院務等官。

translations.literal: Also wealthy households were exhorted and led to relief-sell grain one hundred forty-odd ten thousand shi; all who bestowed rice had the amount of their gift examined for more or less, and were conferred yamen-supervisory and other offices.
translations.idiomatic: The court also urged wealthy households to sell more than 1.4 million shi of relief grain; donors were ranked by the size of their gift and rewarded with posts in the yamen-supervisory service and other offices.

sentences.zh: 是年，又以鈔一十四萬七千餘錠、鹽引五千道、糧三十萬石，賑紹興、慶元、臺州三路饑民。

translations.literal: That year, also with notes one hundred forty-seven thousand-odd ingots, salt certificates five thousand entries, and grain three hundred thousand shi, famine people of Shaoxing, Qingyuan, and Taizhou three circuits were given relief.
translations.idiomatic: That year Shaoxing, Qingyuan, and Taizhou also received relief in 147,000-odd ingots, 5,000 salt certificates, and 300,000 shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 皇慶元年，寧國饑，賑糧兩月。

translations.literal: Huangqing year one, Ningguo suffered famine; relief grain for two months.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Huangqing, Ningguo's famine brought two months' relief grain.

sentences.zh: 自延祐之後，腹裏、江南饑民歲加賑恤，其所賑或以糧，或以鹽引，或以鈔。

translations.literal: From after Yanyou, interior-province and Jiangnan famine people yearly increased in relief and succor; what was given in relief was sometimes grain, sometimes salt certificates, sometimes paper notes.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yanyou era, famine relief in the heartland and Jiangnan grew year by year, paid now in grain, now in salt certificates, now in paper money.

sentences.zh: 京師賑糶之制：至元二十二年始行。

translations.literal: Capital relief-sale system: from Zhiyuan year twenty-two it was first implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Relief grain sales in the capital began in the twenty-second year of Zhiyuan.

sentences.zh: 其法於京城南城設鋪各三所，分遣官吏，發海運之糧，減其市直以賑糶焉。

translations.literal: Its method: in the capital city's south city shops were set up, three each; officials were dispatched separately; sea-transport grain was issued and its market price reduced for relief sale.
translations.idiomatic: Shops were opened in threes across the capital's southern wards; officials were sent to release sea-transported grain at reduced market rates for relief sale.

sentences.zh: 凡白米每石減鈔五兩，南粳米減鈔三兩，歲以為常。

translations.literal: For white rice every shi was reduced five liang in notes; for southern polished rice three liang; yearly this became the constant rule.
translations.idiomatic: White rice was discounted five liang per shi, southern polished rice three liang—a rule renewed every year.

sentences.zh: 成宗元貞元年，以京師米貴，益廣世祖之制，設肆三十所，發糧七萬餘石糶之，白粳米每石中統鈔一十五兩，白米每石一十二兩，糙米每石六兩五錢。

translations.literal: Chengzong Yuanzhen year one, because capital rice was dear, Shizu's system was broadly expanded: thirty market-stalls were set up; grain seventy thousand-odd shi was issued for relief sale—white polished rice every shi fifteen liang of Zhongtong notes, white rice every shi twelve liang, coarse rice every shi six liang five qian.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanzhen 1, as capital rice prices soared, Chengzong widened Kublai's scheme to thirty stalls and released more than 70,000 shi at fifteen liang per shi for white polished rice, twelve for white rice, and six liang five qian for coarse rice.

sentences.zh: 二年，減米肆為一十所，其每年所糶，多至四十餘萬石，少亦不下二十餘萬石。

translations.literal: Year two, rice stalls were reduced to ten; their yearly relief sales reached at most forty-odd ten thousand shi, at least not below twenty-odd ten thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the stalls were cut to ten, yet annual sales still ranged from 200,000 to more than 400,000 shi.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，增兩城米肆為一十五所，每肆日糶米一百石。

translations.literal: Zhida year one, both cities' rice stalls were increased to fifteen; each stall daily relief-sold rice one hundred shi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhida, stalls in both wards rose to fifteen, each selling one hundred shi a day.

sentences.zh: 四年，增所糶米價為中統鈔二十五貫。

translations.literal: Year four, the relief-sold rice price was raised to twenty-five guan of Zhongtong notes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the relief-sale price was set at twenty-five guan in Zhongtong notes.

sentences.zh: 自是每年所糶，率五十餘萬石。

translations.literal: From this time the yearly relief sales, on average, fifty-odd ten thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter annual relief sales averaged more than 500,000 shi.

sentences.zh: 泰定二年，減米價為二十貫。

translations.literal: Taiding year two, the rice price was reduced to twenty guan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taiding the price fell to twenty guan.

sentences.zh: 致和元年，又減為一十五貫云。

translations.literal: Zhihe year one, again reduced to fifteen guan—so ends the account.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhihe 1 it was cut again to fifteen guan.

sentences.zh: 賑糶糧之外，復有紅帖糧。

translations.literal: Beyond relief-sale grain, there was also red-slip grain.
translations.idiomatic: Alongside relief sales ran a second program: red-slip grain.

sentences.zh: 紅帖糧者，成宗大德五年始行。

translations.literal: Red-slip grain: Chengzong Dade year five, first implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Red-slip grain began in the fifth year of Dade under Chengzong.

sentences.zh: 初，賑糶糧多為豪強嗜利之徒，用計巧取，弗能周及貧民。

translations.literal: At first, relief-sale grain was largely taken by powerful families and profit-seeking types who used schemes to seize it cleverly; they could not reach and cover poor people.
translations.idiomatic: At first, relief grain at reduced price was cornered by the powerful and the greedy through artful schemes, never reaching the truly poor.

sentences.zh: 於是令有司籍兩京貧乏戶口之數，置半印號簿文貼，各書其姓名口數，逐月封貼以給。

translations.literal: Thereupon responsible offices were ordered to register both capitals' impoverished household numbers, set half-seal numbered ledger document slips, write each person's name and mouth count, and month by month seal slips for distribution.
translations.idiomatic: Officials then registered the poor of both capitals, issued half-sealed ledger slips bearing each household's name and mouths, and distributed grain monthly against sealed vouchers.

sentences.zh: 大口三斗，小口半之。

translations.literal: Large mouths three dou; small mouths half thereof.
translations.idiomatic: Adults received three dou; children half as much.

sentences.zh: 其價視賑糶之直，三分常減其一，與賑糶並行。

translations.literal: Its price looked to the relief-sale value; of three parts one was constantly reduced, and it ran parallel with relief sale.
translations.idiomatic: The price tracked relief-sale rates but was discounted by a third, operating alongside the public stalls.

sentences.zh: 每年撥米總二十萬四千九百餘石，閏月不與焉。

translations.literal: Every year allocated grain totaled two hundred four thousand nine hundred-odd shi; intercalary months were not included.
translations.idiomatic: The annual allocation totaled 204,900-odd shi, with no issue in intercalary months.

sentences.zh: 其愛民之仁，於此亦可見矣。

translations.literal: Its humane care for the people—in this also can be seen.
translations.idiomatic: Even in such details the dynasty's care for the people is plain to see.

sentences.zh: 入粟補官之制：元初未嘗舉行。

translations.literal: Grain-entry office-supplement system: at the Yuan beginning it was never enacted.
translations.idiomatic: The system of trading grain for office never operated in the dynasty's early years.

sentences.zh: 天歷三年，內外郡縣亢旱為災，於是用太師答剌罕等言，舉而行之。

translations.literal: Tianli year three, inner and outer commands and counties suffered severe drought as disaster; thereupon, on Grand Preceptor Darqan and others' advice, it was enacted and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianli, drought scourged commands and counties alike; at Grand Preceptor Darqan's urging, the policy was finally put into practice.

sentences.zh: 凡江南、陜西、河南等處定為三等，令其富實民戶依例出米，無米者折納價鈔。

translations.literal: All Jiangnan, Shaanxi, Henan, and other places were fixed in three grades; wealthy solid civilian households were ordered to contribute rice according to statute; those without rice converted and paid in valued notes.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan, Shaanxi, Henan, and other regions were divided into three grades, with affluent households required to donate grain or, if they had none, pay the cash equivalent in notes.

sentences.zh: 陜西每石八十兩，河南並腹裏每石六十兩，江南三省每石四十兩，實授茶鹽流官，如不仕讓封父母者聽。

translations.literal: Shaanxi: every shi eighty liang; Henan and the interior: every shi sixty liang; Jiangnan three provinces: every shi forty liang—actually conferring salt-and-tea circulating offices; those who did not take office but yielded titles to ennoble parents were permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Rates were eighty liang per shi in Shaanxi, sixty in Henan and the heartland, and forty in the three Jiangnan provinces, in exchange for substantive posts in the salt-and-tea service; men who declined office to honor parents with rank were allowed to do so.

sentences.zh: 錢谷官考滿，依例升轉。

translations.literal: Revenue-grain officials, upon examination completion, were promoted and transferred according to statute.
translations.idiomatic: Serving revenue-grain officers who completed their term were promoted under the usual rules.

translations.idiomatic: In Shaanxi, 1,500 shi or more earned the Junior Seventh Rank;

translations.literal: above thirty shi, commendation at gate and lane.
translations.idiomatic: 30 shi or more brought commendation at one's gate and lane.

translations.idiomatic: In Henan and the heartland, 2,000 shi or more earned the Junior Seventh Rank;

translations.idiomatic: In the three Jiangnan provinces, 10,000 shi or more earned the Regular Seventh Rank;

sentences.zh: 先已入粟，遙授虛名，今再入粟者，驗其糧數，照依資品，實授茶鹽流官。

translations.literal: Those who had already entered grain and received distant honorary titles—if they now enter grain again, their grain amounts are examined; according to qualification grade they are actually conferred salt-and-tea circulating offices.
translations.idiomatic: Donors who had already contributed grain for remote honorary titles could contribute again; their total was reckoned and a substantive salt-and-tea post conferred by rank.

translations.idiomatic: For Shaanxi repeat donors: 1,000 shi or more, Junior Seventh Rank;

translations.literal: Jiangnan three provinces: above six thousand six hundred sixty shi, regular seventh rank;
translations.idiomatic: In the three Jiangnan provinces: 6,660 shi or more, Regular Seventh Rank;

sentences.zh: 三千三百三十石之上，從七品；

translations.literal: above three thousand three hundred thirty shi, junior seventh rank;
translations.idiomatic: 3,330 shi or more, Junior Seventh Rank;

sentences.zh: 二千石之上，正八品；

translations.literal: above two thousand shi, regular eighth rank;
translations.idiomatic: 2,000 shi or more, Regular Eighth Rank;

sentences.zh: 一千三百三十石之上，從八品；

translations.literal: above one thousand three hundred thirty shi, junior eighth rank;
translations.idiomatic: 1,330 shi or more, Junior Eighth Rank;

sentences.zh: 六百六十石之上，正九品；

translations.literal: above six hundred sixty shi, regular ninth rank;
translations.idiomatic: 660 shi or more, Regular Ninth Rank;

sentences.zh: 三百三十石之上，從九品。

translations.literal: above three hundred thirty shi, junior ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: 330 shi or more, Junior Ninth Rank.

sentences.zh: 先已入粟，實授茶鹽流官，今再入粟者，驗其糧數，加等升除。

translations.literal: Those who had already entered grain and actually received salt-and-tea circulating offices—if they now enter grain again, their grain amounts are examined and they are promoted or demoted by grade.
translations.idiomatic: Donors already holding substantive salt-and-tea posts who contributed again had their total examined and were raised or lowered in grade accordingly.

sentences.zh: 陜西：七百五十石之上，五百石之上，二百五十石之上，一百五十石之上，一百石之上。

translations.literal: Shaanxi: above seven hundred fifty shi, above five hundred shi, above two hundred fifty shi, above one hundred fifty shi, above one hundred shi.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi repeat donors: thresholds at 750, 500, 250, 150, and 100 shi.

sentences.zh: 河南並腹裏：一千石之上，七百五十石之上，五百石之上，二百五十石之上，一百五十石之上。

translations.literal: Henan and the interior: above one thousand shi, above seven hundred fifty shi, above five hundred shi, above two hundred fifty shi, above one hundred fifty shi.
translations.idiomatic: Henan and the heartland: thresholds at 1,000, 750, 500, 250, and 150 shi.

sentences.zh: 僧道入粟：三百石之上，賜六字師號，都省給之；

translations.literal: Monks and Daoists entering grain: above three hundred shi, bestowed a six-character master title, given by the Metropolitan Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Clergy who contributed grain: 300 shi or more earned a six-character honorific title from the Metropolitan Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 二百石之上，四字師號，一百石之上，二字師號，禮部給之。

translations.literal: above two hundred shi, a four-character master title; above one hundred shi, a two-character master title—the Ministry of Rites issued them.
translations.idiomatic: 200 shi or more a four-character title, 100 shi or more a two-character title, both issued by the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 四川省富實民戶，有能入粟赴江陵者，依河南省補官例行之。

translations.literal: Sichuan province's wealthy solid civilian households who could enter grain and proceed to Jiangling were treated according to Henan province's office-supplement precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy households in Sichuan who could deliver grain to Jiangling were ranked under the same rules as Henan.

sentences.zh: 夫入粟補官，雖非先王之政，然荒劄之余，民賴其助者多矣，故特識於篇末而不敢略云。

translations.literal: As for entering grain to supplement office, although it is not the policy of the former kings, yet in the aftermath of famine and ruin many people relied on its aid—therefore it is specially recorded at the chapter's end and not briefly omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Trading grain for office was no policy of the ancient kings, yet after famine and devastation countless people lived by its aid—reason enough to set it down at the chapter's close rather than pass it by in silence.
